form.title: IB Diploma Year 1 Humanities onboarding test

writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: The Great Depression began with
items.answer: the Wall Street Crash of 1929
options: the end of the First World War
items.markingKey: C. the Wall Street Crash of 1929. Share prices collapsed in New York

items.stem: The First World War broke out in
items.markingKey: B. 1914. After the assassination at Sarajevo

items.stem: Why did the war lead to rising prices and hardship in colonies such as India?
items.answer: Colonial economies were taxed and drained to pay for the war
options: Colonial economies were taxed and drained to pay for the war
items.markingKey: B. Colonial economies were taxed and drained to pay for the war. War costs were passed on

items.stem: Hitler became Chancellor of Germany in
items.answer: January 1933
items.markingKey: C. January 1933. Appointed by Hindenburg

items.stem: Which event helped the Nazis win support after 1929?
items.answer: Mass unemployment during the Depression
items.markingKey: D. Mass unemployment during the Depression. Desperate voters turned to extremes

items.stem: How did the Enabling Act of 1933 help Hitler become a dictator?
items.answer: It let him pass laws without the Reichstag
options: It let him pass laws without the Reichstag
items.markingKey: C. It let him pass laws without the Reichstag. Legal route to dictatorship

items.stem: A diary written by a soldier during a battle is a
items.answer: primary source
items.markingKey: A. primary source. Created at the time

items.stem: Why should a government poster from wartime be used with care?
items.answer: It was made to persuade, so it may be one-sided
options: It was made to persuade, so it may be one-sided
It was made long after the war
items.markingKey: A. It was made to persuade, so it may be one-sided. Purpose affects reliability

items.stem: Two eyewitnesses describe the same protest differently. What is the best way for a historian to proceed?
items.answer: Compare both with other evidence and consider who wrote each and why
options: Compare both with other evidence and consider who wrote each and why
items.markingKey: B. Compare both with other evidence and consider who wrote each and why. Corroboration and provenance

items.stem: Which is an example of a long-term cause?
items.answer: decades of economic inequality
items.markingKey: A. decades of economic inequality. Develops over a long period

items.stem: A trigger (immediate cause) is
items.answer: the event that sets off a crisis that was already building
options: the event that sets off a crisis that was already building
items.markingKey: D. the event that sets off a crisis that was already building. The spark

items.stem: Why do historians usually rank causes rather than list them?
items.answer: To judge which causes mattered most and how they interacted
options: To judge which causes mattered most and how they interacted
items.markingKey: A. To judge which causes mattered most and how they interacted. Weighing significance

items.stem: In OPVL, the "O" stands for
items.answer: origin
items.subtopicHint: Source analysis: origin, purpose and content (OPVL)
items.markingKey: D. origin. Who made it, when and where

items.stem: A government press release about a riot has limited value because
items.answer: its purpose may be to defend the government's actions
items.subtopicHint: Source analysis: origin, purpose and content (OPVL)
options: its purpose may be to defend the government's actions
items.markingKey: A. its purpose may be to defend the government's actions. Purpose shapes content

items.stem: A memoir written 40 years after events by a participant. What is one value and one limitation?
items.answer: Value: insider knowledge; limitation: memory and hindsight may distort it
items.subtopicHint: Source analysis: origin, purpose and content (OPVL)
options: Value: insider knowledge; limitation: memory and hindsight may distort it
items.markingKey: C. Value: insider knowledge; limitation: memory and hindsight may distort it. Balance origin and purpose

items.stem: Before independence, Rwanda was ruled by
items.answer: Belgium
items.markingKey: A. Belgium. From 1916

items.stem: How did colonial identity cards affect Rwandan society?
items.answer: They fixed Hutu and Tutsi as rigid ethnic categories
options: They fixed Hutu and Tutsi as rigid ethnic categories
items.markingKey: C. They fixed Hutu and Tutsi as rigid ethnic categories. Divide and rule

items.stem: What role did radio station RTLM play in 1994?
items.answer: It spread propaganda that encouraged violence against Tutsi
options: It spread propaganda that encouraged violence against Tutsi
items.markingKey: C. It spread propaganda that encouraged violence against Tutsi. Media and incitement

items.stem: Kosovo was part of which state before 1999?
items.answer: Yugoslavia (Serbia)
items.subtopicHint: Kosovo: causes and course of the conflict
items.markingKey: B. Yugoslavia (Serbia). An autonomous province

items.stem: Why did Milošević's revocation of Kosovo's autonomy in 1989 raise tensions?
items.answer: It removed self-rule from the Albanian majority
items.subtopicHint: Kosovo: causes and course of the conflict
options: It removed self-rule from the Albanian majority
items.markingKey: A. It removed self-rule from the Albanian majority. Serbian nationalism

items.stem: Why did NATO intervene in 1999 without UN Security Council approval?
items.answer: Russia was expected to veto action, and NATO cited humanitarian grounds
items.subtopicHint: Kosovo: causes and course of the conflict
options: Russia was expected to veto action, and NATO cited humanitarian grounds
items.markingKey: B. Russia was expected to veto action, and NATO cited humanitarian grounds. Contested legality

items.stem: Dividing power between the legislature, executive and judiciary is called
items.answer: separation of powers
items.markingKey: C. separation of powers. Checks and balances

items.stem: In a dictatorship, power is held by
items.answer: one person or a small group without free elections
options: one person or a small group without free elections
items.markingKey: C. one person or a small group without free elections. No accountability

items.stem: Why is a free press important in a democracy?
items.answer: It informs citizens and holds the government to account
options: It informs citizens and holds the government to account
items.markingKey: B. It informs citizens and holds the government to account. Accountability

items.stem: A political party mainly aims to
items.answer: win elections and form a government
options: win elections and form a government
items.markingKey: B. win elections and form a government. Seeking power

items.stem: A coalition government is formed when
items.answer: no single party has a majority, so parties share power
options: no single party has a majority, so parties share power
items.markingKey: A. no single party has a majority, so parties share power. Combining seats

items.stem: Why can proportional representation lead to many coalition governments?
items.answer: Small parties win seats in proportion to votes, so one party rarely has a majority
options: Small parties win seats in proportion to votes, so one party rarely has a majority
It gives all seats to the largest party
items.markingKey: B. Small parties win seats in proportion to votes, so one party rarely has a majority. Fragmented seats

items.stem: Equal treatment of all citizens regardless of religion, caste or gender is
items.answer: equality before the law
items.markingKey: B. equality before the law. A fundamental principle

items.stem: Which is an example of discrimination?
items.answer: Refusing a job to someone because of their religion
options: Refusing a job to someone because of their religion
items.markingKey: C. Refusing a job to someone because of their religion. Unfair treatment of a group

items.stem: Why do democracies protect minority rights even against majority votes?
items.answer: Majority rule must not become oppression of minorities
options: Majority rule must not become oppression of minorities
items.markingKey: A. Majority rule must not become oppression of minorities. Liberal democracy

items.stem: Using military threats or force to get what a state wants is
items.answer: hard power
items.markingKey: D. hard power. Coercion

items.stem: Which is an example of soft power?
items.answer: A country's films and culture being admired abroad
options: A country's films and culture being admired abroad
items.markingKey: C. A country's films and culture being admired abroad. Attraction (Nye)

items.stem: Why might a state combine aid programmes with military alliances?
items.answer: Smart power mixes attraction and coercion to achieve goals
options: Smart power mixes attraction and coercion to achieve goals
items.markingKey: A. Smart power mixes attraction and coercion to achieve goals. Smart power

items.stem: Sovereignty means
items.answer: supreme authority of a state over its territory
options: supreme authority of a state over its territory
items.markingKey: C. supreme authority of a state over its territory. Westphalian principle

items.stem: Which challenges state sovereignty from above?
items.answer: binding rules of supranational bodies such as the EU
options: binding rules of supranational bodies such as the EU
items.markingKey: D. binding rules of supranational bodies such as the EU. Pooling sovereignty

items.stem: Why is Taiwan described as having contested statehood?
items.answer: It governs itself but is not widely recognised as a sovereign state
options: It governs itself but is not widely recognised as a sovereign state
items.markingKey: C. It governs itself but is not widely recognised as a sovereign state. Recognition matters

items.stem: Legitimacy is
items.answer: the acceptance of an authority's right to rule
options: the acceptance of an authority's right to rule
items.markingKey: C. the acceptance of an authority's right to rule. Rightful power

items.stem: According to Weber, which is a source of legitimacy?
items.answer: charismatic authority
items.markingKey: A. charismatic authority. Traditional, charismatic, legal-rational

items.stem: A government wins a flawed election but delivers rapid growth. How might it claim legitimacy?
items.answer: Through performance legitimacy, despite weak procedural legitimacy
options: Through performance legitimacy, despite weak procedural legitimacy
items.markingKey: D. Through performance legitimacy, despite weak procedural legitimacy. Output versus input legitimacy

items.stem: Which organisation is central to global governance?
items.answer: the United Nations
items.markingKey: C. the United Nations. Since 1945

items.stem: Interdependence means
items.answer: states rely on each other economically and politically
options: states rely on each other economically and politically
items.markingKey: B. states rely on each other economically and politically. Mutual dependence

items.stem: Why is collective action on climate change hard?
items.answer: Each state may free-ride, hoping others will bear the costs
options: Each state may free-ride, hoping others will bear the costs
items.markingKey: C. Each state may free-ride, hoping others will bear the costs. Collective action problem

items.stem: Sustainable development means
items.answer: meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs
options: meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs
items.markingKey: D. meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Brundtland definition

items.stem: Farming mainly to feed the farmer's own family is
items.answer: subsistence farming
items.markingKey: D. subsistence farming. Self-consumption

items.stem: Why is irrigation important for farming in areas with a seasonal monsoon?
items.answer: It supplies water during the dry months
options: It supplies water during the dry months
items.markingKey: D. It supplies water during the dry months. Reliable water

items.stem: Water scarcity can be caused by
items.answer: over-use and pollution as well as low rainfall
options: over-use and pollution as well as low rainfall
items.markingKey: D. over-use and pollution as well as low rainfall. Physical and human causes

items.stem: Rainwater harvesting helps by
items.answer: collecting and storing rain for later use or recharging groundwater
options: collecting and storing rain for later use or recharging groundwater
items.markingKey: B. collecting and storing rain for later use or recharging groundwater. Local solution

items.stem: Why can large dams be controversial?
items.answer: They provide water and power but can displace people and harm ecosystems
options: They provide water and power but can displace people and harm ecosystems
items.markingKey: A. They provide water and power but can displace people and harm ecosystems. Costs and benefits

items.stem: Moving from the countryside to a city is
items.answer: rural-to-urban migration
items.markingKey: C. rural-to-urban migration. Internal movement

items.stem: Which is a pull factor of a city?
items.answer: better job opportunities
items.markingKey: D. better job opportunities. Attracts migrants

items.stem: Why can migration benefit the source country?
items.answer: Migrants send remittances home
items.markingKey: B. Migrants send remittances home. Money transfers

items.stem: Population density is
items.answer: the number of people per square kilometre
options: the number of people per square kilometre
items.markingKey: A. the number of people per square kilometre. People per area

items.stem: In stage 2 of the demographic transition model,
items.answer: death rates fall while birth rates stay high
options: death rates fall while birth rates stay high
items.markingKey: A. death rates fall while birth rates stay high. Rapid growth

items.stem: Why do some countries reach stage 5 of the DTM with a shrinking population?
items.answer: Birth rates fall below death rates as people have fewer children
options: Birth rates fall below death rates as people have fewer children
items.markingKey: C. Birth rates fall below death rates as people have fewer children. Low fertility

items.stem: A population pyramid shows
items.answer: the age and sex structure of a population
options: the age and sex structure of a population
items.markingKey: C. the age and sex structure of a population. Age-sex graph

items.stem: The dependency ratio compares
items.answer: dependants (young and old) with the working-age population
options: dependants (young and old) with the working-age population
items.markingKey: A. dependants (young and old) with the working-age population. Economic burden

items.stem: What challenges does an ageing population create?
items.answer: Higher pension and health costs with fewer workers to pay taxes
options: Higher pension and health costs with fewer workers to pay taxes
items.markingKey: D. Higher pension and health costs with fewer workers to pay taxes. Greying society

items.stem: People forced to leave their country because of persecution are
items.answer: refugees
items.markingKey: B. refugees. Protected by international law

items.stem: Brain drain means
items.answer: skilled workers leaving a country
items.markingKey: C. skilled workers leaving a country. Loss of talent

items.stem: How can international migration help host countries?
items.answer: Migrants fill labour shortages and pay taxes
options: Migrants fill labour shortages and pay taxes
items.markingKey: B. Migrants fill labour shortages and pay taxes. Economic contribution

items.stem: Incoming solar radiation is called
items.answer: insolation
items.subtopicHint: Atmospheric energy and the greenhouse effect
items.markingKey: B. insolation. Incoming sunlight

items.stem: Albedo is
items.answer: the proportion of sunlight reflected by a surface
items.subtopicHint: Atmospheric energy and the greenhouse effect
options: the proportion of sunlight reflected by a surface
items.markingKey: B. the proportion of sunlight reflected by a surface. Reflectivity

items.stem: Why does melting Arctic sea ice speed up warming?
items.answer: Darker ocean absorbs more sunlight than reflective ice
items.subtopicHint: Atmospheric energy and the greenhouse effect
options: Darker ocean absorbs more sunlight than reflective ice
items.markingKey: C. Darker ocean absorbs more sunlight than reflective ice. Positive feedback

items.stem: Per capita income is
items.answer: total national income divided by population
options: total national income divided by population
items.markingKey: A. total national income divided by population. Average income

items.stem: Farming and mining are part of the
items.answer: primary sector
items.markingKey: A. primary sector. Natural resources

items.stem: As countries develop, the share of workers in the tertiary sector usually
items.answer: rises
items.markingKey: C. rises. Services grow

items.stem: Goods bought from other countries are
items.answer: imports
items.markingKey: B. imports. Coming in

items.stem: A tax on imported goods is a
items.answer: tariff
items.markingKey: C. tariff. It makes imports dearer

items.stem: Why might cheaper imported toys harm small domestic toy makers?
items.answer: Consumers may switch to the cheaper imports
options: Consumers may switch to the cheaper imports
items.markingKey: D. Consumers may switch to the cheaper imports. Competition

items.stem: Money solves the problem of the double coincidence of wants because it
items.answer: is a medium of exchange
items.markingKey: A. is a medium of exchange. Barter needs matching wants

items.stem: Which is a likely effect of rising inequality?
items.answer: A larger gap between rich and poor households
options: A larger gap between rich and poor households
items.markingKey: C. A larger gap between rich and poor households. Distribution widens

items.stem: Why can easy access to cheap credit help poor rural families?
items.answer: They can invest in seeds or tools without falling into debt traps
options: They can invest in seeds or tools without falling into debt traps
items.markingKey: D. They can invest in seeds or tools without falling into debt traps. Formal credit is cheaper

items.stem: The basic economic problem arises because
items.answer: wants are unlimited but resources are scarce
options: wants are unlimited but resources are scarce
items.markingKey: A. wants are unlimited but resources are scarce. Scarcity forces choice

items.stem: The next best alternative given up when making a choice is the
items.answer: opportunity cost
items.markingKey: A. opportunity cost. Cost of the forgone option

items.stem: A point inside a production possibility frontier shows
items.answer: unemployed or inefficiently used resources
items.markingKey: A. unemployed or inefficiently used resources. More could be produced

items.stem: The law of demand says that as price falls, quantity demanded
items.answer: rises
items.markingKey: A. rises. Other things equal

items.stem: A rise in income increases demand for a normal good. On a graph, this
items.answer: shifts the demand curve to the right
options: shifts the demand curve to the right
items.markingKey: B. shifts the demand curve to the right. A change in a non-price factor

items.stem: The price of tea rises. What happens to demand for coffee and for sugar?
items.answer: Coffee demand rises; sugar demand falls
options: Coffee demand rises; sugar demand falls
items.markingKey: C. Coffee demand rises; sugar demand falls. Coffee is a substitute, sugar a complement

items.stem: At equilibrium, quantity demanded
items.answer: equals quantity supplied
items.markingKey: C. equals quantity supplied. Market clears

items.stem: If price is below equilibrium there is
items.answer: excess demand (a shortage)
items.markingKey: C. excess demand (a shortage). Buyers want more than is offered

items.stem: A government sets a maximum rent below the equilibrium. What is the likely result?
items.answer: A shortage of rental housing
items.markingKey: A. A shortage of rental housing. Price ceiling

items.stem: If demand is price elastic, a price rise causes
items.answer: a proportionately larger fall in quantity demanded
options: a proportionately larger fall in quantity demanded
items.markingKey: C. a proportionately larger fall in quantity demanded. PED > 1

items.stem: Price rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 5%. What is PED?
Why is demand for salt usually price inelastic?
items.answer: It is a necessity with few substitutes and a small share of income
options: It is a necessity with few substitutes and a small share of income
items.markingKey: A. It is a necessity with few substitutes and a small share of income. Determinants of PED

items.stem: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it

items.stem: Money doubles in 6 years at a fixed compound rate. In how many years does it become 8 times?
Boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 6 more boys join, the ratio is 1 : 1. How many students were there at first?
One pipe fills a tank in 6 hours; another empties it in 9 hours. If both are open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
items.answer: 18 hours

items.stem: Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'?
items.answer: found everywhere

items.stem: Author is to novel as composer is to ...
items.answer: symphony

items.stem: Some economists are writers. All writers are readers. Which statement must be true?
items.answer: Some economists are readers
items.explanation: The economists who are writers are also readers

items.stem: Claim: 'Since the new study app launched, the school's test scores rose, so the app raised scores.' Which fact, if true, most weakens the claim?
options: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
Students said they liked the app
items.answer: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
items.explanation: Another change at the same time offers a different explanation

items.stem: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, ?
items.answer: DW
items.explanation: First letters go forward, second letters go backward

items.stem: What comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?

items.answer: an unshaded hexagon

items.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:15?
items.explanation: The hour hand has moved a quarter of 30° past the 3

items.explanation: One at the centre of each face
